description: Section 02, and the page's one light surface. It carries the most body copy, which is where dark-on-light actually helps someone read.
name: About

description: The standing facts. A fact with no value is the rotating one, so 'previously based in' has a list behind it rather than a single answer.
name: AboutFacts

description: Section 04. Three paragraphs and one rotating frame, cut down from six captioned cards that were more structure than the content had.
name: Adventures

description: The advisory offer. The specifics sit inside a details element: someone scanning needs the offer, someone who wants the scope will open it.
name: AdvisoryCard

description: The places she has lived, cycling one at a time on the same eight-second slot as the photographs so it does not drift against them.
name: CityRotator

description: Editor-installed layout for the component-isolation surface. Returns 404 in production so the isolation routes are never reachable from the live site.
name: CodeYamIsolateLayout

untestabilityReason.justification: Installed by codeyam-editor rather than authored here. It is a template shell whose only logic is the production 404 guard; it renders no product surface of its own.

description: Section 06. The note form and the profiles share one destination because they answer the same reader question.
name: Contact

description: The note form. On success it is replaced by a confirmation, which makes a duplicate send impossible; on failure the draft is kept and the profiles are offered, since there is deliberately no email address on the site.
name: ContactForm

description: Section 05. Press, essays, and awards in reverse chronological order, so it reads as a timeline rather than a filing cabinet.
name: Elsewhere

description: One Elsewhere entry: kind, title, venue, year. A few entries have a second home, which hangs off the row rather than duplicating it.
name: ElsewhereRow

description: The arrow marking a link as leaving the site.
name: ExternalLinkIcon

description: A labelled control and the message shown when it needs a look. The control is passed as children rather than described by props, because the three fields differ in type, autocomplete, and element.
name: Field

description: Where else to find her, and where she is. It shares the section with the form rather than standing alone.
name: FindMe

description: Footer navigation and the signoff, with the brand linked in place inside the authored sentence.
name: Footer

description: The signoff with the brand linked in place. The copy is authored as one sentence rather than assembled from fragments, so the link is found inside it via splitOnBrand; if the brand is ever edited out, the sentence still renders whole.
name: FooterSignoff

description: Shown when a note did not send. It says nothing was lost, because nothing was, and offers the profiles as another route since there is deliberately no email address on the site.
name: FormFailure

description: The opening screen: full-bleed rotating photography, a headline that types itself in, and a cue naming the section below.
name: Hero

description: The full-bleed rotation behind the hero headline.
name: HeroBackdrop

description: Hidden from people, irresistible to bots. A filled value is answered silently, because telling a bot it was detected only teaches whoever wrote it to leave the field alone.
name: Honeypot

description: The header and the indicator showing which section you are in. The number sits left of the label, mirroring the section heads, and is positioned into the existing gap so nothing reflows when it appears.
name: Nav

description: The section links. The number sits to the left of the label, mirroring the section heads, and is absolutely positioned into the gap that already exists between items so nothing reflows when it appears and no space is reserved when nothing is active.
name: NavLinks

description: The wordmark linking back to the top of the page.
name: NavMark

description: What a visitor to a URL that does not exist sees: the 404 eyebrow, the statement, and the way back. Deliberately no explanation of what went wrong — the design system asks for restraint over helpfulness. Renders the body only; the 404 status comes from Next.js serving app/not-found.tsx.
name: NotFound

description: The Next.js not-found route. Composition only: it returns <NotFound /> and declares the page metadata, including robots noindex so a crawler that reaches a dead URL drops it rather than indexing it.
name: NotFoundPage

untestabilityReason.justification: Returns <NotFound /> and nothing else, so its rendered output is identical to the NotFound component scenario notfound-default; a second capture would duplicate that image. An application scenario at the real route was attempted and is structurally impossible here: this page's CORRECT response is HTTP 404, and the capture pipeline treats a 404 as a failed capture — it settled, restarted the dev server, retried, then refused, leaving a screenshot-less ghost scenario that had to be deleted. Its only non-visual surface is the static metadata export.

description: The contact endpoint. Answers the honeypot silently so a bot learns nothing, then writes the row before attempting delivery, so a message survives a mail outage with emailedAt left null rather than being lost. Validation logic lives in validateMessage and is tested there.
name: POST

untestabilityReason.justification: A Next route handler over the network and Prisma boundaries. Its decision logic is extracted into validateMessage, which is covered directly; what remains here is request parsing, persistence, and status codes.

description: The site's only route. It is composition alone: the nav, the six numbered sections in reading order inside a main landmark, then the footer. Every section owns its own copy and photography.
name: Page

description: Cross-fades photographs on a shared eight-second slot, so every rotation on the page lands on one beat instead of something always being mid-fade. Frames are pre-cropped to the container's aspect, so nothing is enlarged or trimmed at render time.
name: PhotoRotator

description: Recent essays, dated so the list reads as a timeline.
name: PostList

description: The document shell. It carries the metadata and canonical URL for nadiaeldeib.com and loads the token stylesheet. The palette is deliberately not behind prefers-color-scheme: the dark surface is the design, not a preference.
name: RootLayout

untestabilityReason.justification: The Next.js document shell. It renders html and body around children and sets static metadata; there is no branching to exercise, and the page it wraps is covered by the home-full-page scenario.

description: Editor-installed route that resolves a scenario slug to its real URL and redirects there, so a scenario can be opened by slug alone.
name: ScenarioRedirectPage

untestabilityReason.justification: Installed by codeyam-editor rather than authored here. It reads scenarios.json off disk and redirects; it renders no product surface, so there is nothing visual to capture.

description: The cue into the first section. It names where it goes rather than saying scroll, because what is below is more compelling than the instruction.
name: ScrollCue

description: The numbered eyebrow every section carries. The number is information, not decoration: the sections are a sequence and the nav indicator mirrors this exact pairing.
name: SectionHead

description: Replaces the form once a note lands, which is the clearest signal it worked and makes a duplicate send impossible.
name: SentConfirmation

description: The profiles, ordered the way she actually uses them.
name: SocialList

description: The closed set of reasons someone might be writing. The ids come from the content file and are the same list the server validates against.
name: TopicChips

description: The headline that types itself in via a clip-path reveal on a steps() function, with the cursor riding the same function so it sits on the text edge. The step count is the line's own character count, so it cannot fall out of sync with the words.
name: TypedHeadline

description: Section 01. Opens on the north star, then what she is building at CodeYam, the links out, and the advisory offer.
name: Work

description: External links, each showing its destination host so the target is never a surprise.
name: WorkLinkList

description: The Work prose column. The north star leads and the subhead then names what she is building, so the reader gets the why before the what.
name: WorkNarrative

description: Section 03. What she writes about, the way through to the full archive, and a few recent essays.
name: Writing

description: What she writes about, and the link through to everything else.
name: WritingIntro

description: Shapes the Customer.io wire body for one note: subject from topic and sender, plain-text and escaped HTML parts, recipient identifiers, and reply_to set to the person who wrote in rather than the site's sending address.
name: buildSendPayload

description: Renders a saved message as the plain-text note: sender, topic, optional source page and message id first, then the sender's own words last and unwrapped so a long message is not pushed below a wall of metadata.
name: composeBody

description: The 500 reply for a failed write. Says nothing was sent, which is literally true and tells the sender to retry rather than assume the note arrived.
name: couldNotSave

description: Attempts delivery of a saved note and stamps emailedAt strictly AFTER the provider accepts, never before and never on a failed send. Returns delivered, not-delivered, or delivered-unstamped. emailedAt is the only record of whether a note reached the inbox, so stamping optimistically would make an undelivered note indistinguishable from a delivered one. Takes its collaborators as arguments so all three outcomes are reachable without a database or a mail provider.
name: deliverAndStamp

description: Turns a rejected provider response into an operator-readable reason, carrying the provider's own text because that is what separates a bad token from an unverified recipient. Truncated for a log line, and survives a body that cannot be read.
name: describeSendFailure

description: Escapes ampersand and angle brackets so an untrusted note cannot alter the structure of the HTML part. Ampersand is replaced first, or the escapes themselves would be re-escaped into visible garbage.
name: escapeHtml

description: Reports whether the hidden company field came back filled in. Whitespace does not count, since a stray space from an autofill would otherwise silently discard a real person's message while telling them it succeeded.
name: isHoneypotTripped

description: Seeds the Message table with the received-messages world used by the home-full-page scenario, so a capture shows a coherent inbox rather than leftover state.
name: main

untestabilityReason.justification: A seed script whose whole body is Prisma writes against the database; it computes nothing and returns nothing to assert on.

description: The 422 reply carrying per-field problems so the form can point at what needs fixing. 422 rather than 400: the request was understood, its contents were not acceptable.
name: needsAnotherLook

description: Picks the active section from document order and the set of currently visible ids. Sections are contiguous so two can briefly both cross the observer band; document order breaks the tie, which keeps the nav indicator moving forward instead of flickering between neighbours.
name: pickActive

description: Parses an untrusted request body into a result rather than throwing or returning a response, so parsing holds no opinion about HTTP. Malformed input is an expected arrival on a public endpoint, not an exceptional one.
name: readJsonBody

description: Reads the three variables a send requires and reports which are missing by NAME, never by value. Treats an empty string as unset so a blank placeholder in an env file is not mistaken for configuration.
name: readMailConfig

description: Reads the seed message fixture from the same file the scenario captures use, so a local database and a captured screenshot look at identical data. Returns an empty list when the file is absent or unreadable: a clone that only wants a running site does not need the demo inbox, and an empty table is a valid state.
name: readSeedMessages

untestabilityReason.justification: Reads a fixed project path via readFileSync with no injection point, so neither the success path nor the missing-file fallback can be varied from a test. The transforms applied to what it returns are covered in prisma/seedRows.test.ts.

description: Reads DATABASE_URL and throws a message naming .env.local and DATABASE.md when it is absent or empty. Shared by the Next.js client singleton and the standalone seed script so the two entry points cannot drift; Postgres has no local-file fallback, so failing here rather than at first query is what turns a cryptic driver error into an actionable one.
name: requireConnectionString

description: Generates robots.txt: every crawler may read the whole site, and the sitemap is advertised on the canonical host so no fetch pays a redirect hop. Nothing is disallowed on purpose — the editor's isolation routes already 404 in production, and robots.txt is public, so naming them would advertise paths rather than hide them.
name: robots

description: The 201 reply carrying the new row id, returned whether or not the email went out, because the row exists either way and delivery is not the sender's problem.
name: saved

description: Delivers one contact-form note to the configured inbox through Customer.io's transactional API. Never throws: the row is already saved by the time it runs, so a delivery failure comes back as a result to record rather than an exception. The only module that reads CONTACT_INBOX, which it never logs or returns.
name: sendNotification

description: Picks the Customer.io regional host, defaulting to US and switching to the EU deployment only on CUSTOMERIO_REGION=eu. The hosts are separate deployments and a token issued in one is rejected by the other, so the default is a real failure mode rather than cosmetics.
name: sendUrl

description: The honeypot reply, deliberately indistinguishable from success in both status and body shape. Telling a bot it was detected only teaches whoever wrote it to leave the field alone next time.
name: silentlyAccepted

description: Joins the site's canonical origin (the SITE_URL constant in this file — the bare apex over https) to a root-relative path without producing a doubled slash, returning the bare origin for the site root whether asked by default or explicitly as '/'. The origin is stated once here because three consumers must agree on it — document metadata, robots.txt and sitemap.xml — and because four hostnames reach the app while only the apex is advertised, the other three being 301s. Exists rather than a template literal at each call site because a path passed without its leading slash would otherwise concatenate into nadiaeldeib.comsitemap.xml.
name: siteUrl

description: Generates sitemap.xml with the single entry the site actually has. The six numbered sections are anchors within '/', not routes, so listing them would offer crawlers several URLs resolving to one document. If the site ever grows a real second route, it belongs here.
name: sitemap

description: Splits an authored sentence around the first occurrence of a brand name so it can be linked in place. The signoff stays one piece of copy instead of being assembled from fragments, and reassembly is exact.
name: splitOnBrand

description: Coerces an untrusted JSON value to a trimmed string, collapsing anything that is not a string to empty so a number or object can never reach a length check.
name: str

description: Posts the contact form and classifies the response into the three outcomes the form acts on: replace itself with a confirmation, mark individual fields, or keep the draft and offer the profiles as another route. A thrown fetch is reported without blaming the visitor's connection.
name: submitMessage

description: Builds the seed script's one-line report, counting delivered against undelivered so the seeded undelivered row stays visible in the output.
name: summarize

description: Maps one seed record to a database row. Leaves createdAt undefined when absent so the column default applies, while emailedAt is explicitly null: the two absences mean different things, and a null emailedAt is the seeded record of a note that arrived but was never delivered.
name: toMessageRow

description: The 400 reply for a body that could not be parsed at all.
name: unreadableRequest

description: Reports which section the reader is in, via an IntersectionObserver band about 40 percent down the viewport. Replaced a CSS scroll timeline that flipped states when a section did not fill the viewport, which read as the nav number blinking. The choice of which visible section wins is pickActive, which is covered by unit tests; the subscription itself is exercised by the Nav scenario.
name: useActiveSection

description: Reports whether the page has scrolled past a fraction of the viewport height, batching reads into an animation frame so a fast scroll does not thrash layout. Drives the nav bar going solid.
name: useScrolledPast

untestabilityReason.justification: Reads window.scrollY and window.innerHeight and schedules via requestAnimationFrame; none of those exist in the node test environment.

description: Validates an inbound contact message and returns every problem at once, so the form can mark all bad fields in one pass rather than one reload at a time. The topic allow-list is derived from the content file rather than restated, which is what fixes the drift that made the form's own default chip come back 422.
name: validateMessage
